note: Cross-repo projection lock for the ontos-data-json/1 profile (docs/spec/ontos-data-json.md). These are DERIVATION vectors, not schema-validation: each valid case pins a domain-JSON document -> ontos-data-json/1 projection -> ontos/data value -> ontos-codec-v1 bytes -> SHA-256 (codecSha256, the 'inner' digest), and the domain-separated era-2 preimage Tuple(Atom(tag), value) -> ontos-codec-v1 -> SHA-256 (era2.digest). The pin is the PAIR (ontos-data-json/1, ontos-codec-v1): the projection profile and the codec version are independent coordinates (map/set entry order is codec-version-relative). Every expectation here is HARNESS-DERIVED by the differential oracle over the frozen tri-core data+codec libraries (not hand-authored, none provisional); the deep byte corpus (full projected value trees + full hex) lives in the sibling vectors/data-json.oracle.json, pinned by sha256 below so it is reachable and drift-evident without the 155KB blob crossing repos. Reproduction per case: project the doc -> value tree, then `ontos canon --emit --from-json - < tree.json | xxd -r -p | sha256sum` (inner); wrap Tuple(Atom(<tag>), value) and canon --emit that for the era-2 digest. VALID-case `doc` is a live JSON value (lossless: pure int/string/bool/object/array). REJECT-case `doc` is given as RAW JSON SOURCE text (`docSource`) so the exact number literal under test survives — a parsed JSON number cannot distinguish 1e3 from 1000.0. The same raw-source discipline has a hard limit this corpus cannot cross: this file is itself JSON and must remain well-formed UTF-8, so a document whose defect is raw invalid UTF-8 BYTES inside a string literal is unrepresentable here — only the escape form of a text-fidelity defect (an unpaired surrogate, `\ud800`) can ride in a vector. The raw-byte form of the same defect (ontos-internal#216, same outcome class: the producer must reject rather than succeed with a different admissible datum) is pinned by unit tests in each face whose input type can construct it; its absence from this corpus is this constraint, not an oversight. ONE exception to the oracle-derivation provenance: the depth-floor boundary case (corpusKey depth-floor-512, ontos-internal#236) pins the resource-limit posture’s minimum-accept depth; its digests are tri-face-derived (each face’s suite recomputes and agrees) but it lives outside the sibling oracle blob, whose corpus predates the posture. Add-only revision discipline: a future ontos-data-json/2 may only assign a reading to a form /1 REJECTS (e.g. the reserved decimal arm exercised below); it never re-points an arm /1 accepts, so every digest here is drift-proof by construction.

corpus.note: deep corpus: per-document full projected value tree + inner codec-v1 hex + domain-separated preimage hex; produced by the same oracle run that derived the digests here.

valid.desc: projects a mind.v0 class binding declaration (all nodes object/array/string/integer-literal/bool — no fraction/exponent/null, so projection is total) and domain-separates under the bind2 era-2 tag

events.semantics: self-observations (tool/brain/journal/obligations). Drained on ANY exit - a crashed turn's observations are still facts - unlike outbox, whose commit rides the exit block.

STATE_DIR.semantics: membrane root override — injected by a host/certifier that relocates the membrane (tests, certification); a body must read it through the generated binding accessor only

brainApiKey.semantics: the brain credential for the account bound at Create; value host-held, materialized late, never present in any declaration/record/plan; rotation requires recreation (snapshot phase)

valid.desc: projects a kind-declaration (soil-sample) with the top-level `description` field stripped per the decl-era preimage rule, then domain-separates under the decl2 era-2 tag; schema bounds minimum:0 / maximum:14 are INTEGER literals reading as int (not rejected)

value.note: `doc` is the projection input (description already removed); the original declaration carried a top-level description string, stripped before projection per anvil's decl2 preimage rule.

valid.desc: projects a protocol declaration (title/required/properties — all object/array/string, projection total) with NO preprocess strip, then domain-separates under the pdecl2 era-2 tag; twin-witnessed cross-repo byte-identical against the kernel ProtocolDeclarationDigest2

value.note: no preprocess: unlike decl2 (strip top-level `description`) / rel2 (strip top-level `release`), the pdecl2 family strips nothing, so the era-2 preimage covers the whole declaration. The map arms sort by encoded-key bytes (length-prefix first): title(5) < required(8) < properties(10), not lexicographic.

valid.desc: projects a release descriptor (body-envelope.v2 — bindingDigest/class/classDeclaration/declarationDigest/descriptorVersion/image/imageArtifactId, all object/string, projection total) with the top-level `release` field stripped per the rel-era preimage rule, then domain-separates under the rel2 era-2 tag; twin-witnessed cross-repo byte-identical against the kernel ReleaseRootDigest2

value.note: `doc` is the projection input (release already removed); the original descriptor carried a top-level `release` object, stripped before projection per anvil's rel2 preimage rule — the same strip discipline as decl2's `description`. The map arms sort by encoded-key bytes (length-prefix first), so class(5) < image(5, tie broken by content) precedes the longer keys; the era-2 preimage covers the stripped descriptor under the rel2 tag.

valid.desc: projects a kind-vector suite descriptor (forge.kind-vectors/1 — cases/description/forDeclaration/harnessContract, all string, projection total), DESCRIPTION-INCLUSIVE (the vec2 family strips nothing), then domain-separates under the vec2 era-2 tag; twin-witnessed cross-repo byte-identical against the kernel VectorSuiteDigest2

value.note: no preprocess: unlike decl2 (strip top-level `description`) / rel2 (strip top-level `release`), the vec2 family strips nothing — it is DESCRIPTION-INCLUSIVE, so the era-2 preimage covers the whole suite descriptor including `description`. The map arms sort by encoded-key bytes (length-prefix first): cases(5) < description(11) < forDeclaration(14) < harnessContract(15), not lexicographic.

valid.desc: projects a build manifest (manifestVersion/sourceRoot/entries, where entries is a list of {path,digest} objects, all string, projection total), then domain-separates under the manif2 era-2 tag; the manif2 family strips nothing; twin-witnessed cross-repo byte-identical against the kernel ManifestDigest2

value.note: no preprocess: the manif2 family strips nothing, so the era-2 preimage covers the whole manifest. manifestVersion is the STRING "1" (utf8-text), not an int — the int arm is never taken here. Top map keys sort by encoded-key bytes (length-prefix first): entries(7) < sourceRoot(10) < manifestVersion(15); each entry's keys: path(4) < digest(6).

valid.desc: the resource-limit posture's MINIMUM-ACCEPT depth (spec floor 512, ontos-internal#236): a 512-deep array MUST be accepted by every conformant face. Faces bound nesting (Go 10000, TS 1024, Rust 512 — per-face, stated, never pinned here); rejection above a face's ceiling is the LIMIT class, distinct from domain rejection, so this corpus pins only the floor's ACCEPT side. The era-2 tag probe1 is synthetic — it pins the wrap arithmetic, not a registered domain tag

reject.desc: a fraction number literal is REJECTED path-named (reserved decimal arm ungraduated under /1) — never coerced to a float or decimal

reject.reason: non-integer number literal "3.14" — fraction/exponent rejected under ontos-data-json/1 (reserved decimal arm ungraduated)

reject.desc: an exponent number literal is REJECTED path-named (same reserved-decimal-arm rule) — the raw `1e3` lexical form is preserved via docSource so the literal, not its normalized value, is what is tested

reject.reason: non-integer number literal "1e3" — fraction/exponent rejected under ontos-data-json/1 (reserved decimal arm ungraduated)

reject.desc: a string containing an unpaired surrogate is REJECTED path-named — it has NO UTF-8 encoding, and a decoder that substitutes U+FFFD SUCCEEDS WITH A DIFFERENT ADMISSIBLE DATUM (ontos-data.md §4.1 law 2, the fidelity law), the one outcome an identity-digest projection must never produce. This corner being unlocked is exactly how the Go and TS faces drifted silently (ontos-internal#216: Go's encoding/json coerced and succeeded; TS rejected). docSource carries the escape form (\ud800) because this file must itself remain valid UTF-8; the paired escape \ud83d\ude00 before it MUST combine to one code point (U+1F600, 2 UTF-16 units), pinning both the pairing rule and the UTF-16 unit count in the reported index (soil- is 5 units, the emoji 2, the hyphen 1 → index 8). The raw-invalid-byte form of the same defect is unrepresentable in a JSON-hosted vector and is covered by unit tests in the Go face

reject.reason: unpaired surrogate 0xd800 at UTF-16 index 8 — the string has no UTF-8 encoding, rejected under ontos-data-json/1 (U+FFFD coercion violates the ontos-data.md §4.1 fidelity law)

duplicateKeys.note: ontos-internal#322 — the SOURCE-ADMISSION axis over the same /1 mapping. The profile projects a repeated object member last-wins (docs/spec/ontos-data-json.md §The projection, *Duplicate object keys*), and a face MAY offer an opt-in `duplicateKeys: reject` mode that refuses the document instead of collapsing it. These cases pin that mode's OUTCOME CLASS and LOCATION, never a reason string: for each `reject` case the strict mode refuses at `path` (the repeated member — the FIRST repeat in source order, in the same `$.key` / `$[i]` spelling as the reject cases above) naming `key` (the member name AS DECODED: an escaped and a literal spelling of one name collide; two names that differ in bytes do not, even when canonically equivalent — no normalization, ontos-data §5.2), while the DEFAULT mode accepts the same document and projects it to the SAME ontos-codec-v1 bytes as `lastWinsEquivalent` — the document with the repeated members already collapsed, hand-written — which the strict mode in turn accepts to those same bytes. `accept` cases are duplicate-free under the exact-content rule and must project byte-identically in both modes. No digests here, deliberately: each claim is an equivalence between two documents under ONE face, which needs no oracle and cannot drift with one. Every `valid` and `reject` case above also holds UNCHANGED under the strict mode — the number-literal, text-fidelity, trailing-data and depth-limit outcome classes are not touched by the policy — and each face's suite replays them through it. Hand-authored from the spec.

reject.desc: a repeated member at the root is refused at that member; the default mode keeps the LAST value
an escaped spelling of a name collides with its literal spelling — the rule is exact DECODED content, so \u0061 IS a
a repeat inside a nested object is refused at the nested member path, even when both values are EQUAL — the defect is the repetition, not a conflict
a repeat inside an object that sits in an array is refused at the indexed path
a supplementary-plane name spelled as a surrogate-pair escape collides with its literal spelling — the pair combines to ONE code point before comparison
three occurrences refuse at the FIRST repeat (the second occurrence); the default mode keeps the third
the same name in a CHILD object between the two occurrences is a different object's member and does not reset the count — the root repeat is still refused
the empty name is a name like any other: repeating it is refused, and the path is `$.` with an empty last segment

accept.desc: the same name in two DIFFERENT objects is not a repeat
canonically equivalent but byte-distinct names stay distinct — U+00E9 vs e + U+0301; the projection never normalizes (ontos-data §5.2), so strict mode must not either
names differing only in case are distinct
a name reused by a nested child is not a repeat of the parent's member
identical sibling objects in an array each carry their own member set
an empty object and an empty document-level array have nothing to repeat
